audit.title: CCIP API | CCIP Tools Reference
audit.contentType: developer documentation / REST API reference landing page

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong opener: "REST API for querying cross-chain message data, lane information, and intent operations on the Chainlink Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol." Base URL/Version/Format/License are liftable facts up top. Sections lead with their answer. Minor: no one-line "what is CCIP" for context.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Two clean tables, logical H2 progression, median 46 words/section — ideal RAG chunks.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured facts show 1 prose numeral and the vague quantifier "most." No rate-limit thresholds, no latency figures, no per-chain specifics despite a Multi-Chain section. Version 2.0.0 and "9 languages" are the only real numbers.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Adequate for an index (28 internal links, good hub structure) but 0 primary/authoritative external links. No link to a CCIP concept/spec page or the OpenAPI spec.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The lead sentence and Authentication statement ("Most CCIP API endpoints are publicly accessible and do not require authentication") are cleanly liftable. CCIP acronym is expanded. Fine.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Canonical URL, rich og/twitter tags, and clean semantic headings present. But JSON-LD is only `BreadcrumbList` — no `APIReference`/`TechArticle` schema — and `dateModified`/`datePublished` are absent, so engines get no freshness signal.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weakest dimension. The single fenced block is untagged and corrupted: `# Example: Check response status in scriptscurl -s ...` has collapsed newlines, fusing the comment into the command. Not copy-pasteable; an agent would emit broken shell.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: The Quick Reference table matches intent well ("Track a cross-chain message"), and HTTP Status Codes + Authentication cover part of the debug lifecycle. Missing: symptom-phrased headings and any FAQ/troubleshooting for error strings agents actually query.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming of CCIP, lanes, intents, messages. No undefined jargon.

audit.summary: This is a concise, well-structured index page for the CCIP REST API that opens with a clean canonical definition and a scannable Quick Reference table mapping use cases to endpoints. Its biggest GEO strength is structural clarity (5 sections, no level skips, two extraction-ready tables); its biggest opportunity is the single broken/untagged code block and the near-total absence of concrete numbers (rate limits, latencies) — the page says "be mindful of rate limits" without stating any. The honest verdict: solid retrieval scaffolding, but a generative engine lifting the curl example would quote mangled code, and agents asking "what are the rate limits" get no answer.

recommendations.title: Fix the corrupted curl code block
recommendations.where: HTTP Status Codes section, the "Bash" fenced block
recommendations.change: Restore newlines and tag the fence ```` ```bash ````: ```bash # Check response status code curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \ "https://api.ccip.chain.link/v2/message/0x..." ```
recommendations.why: Engines and agents lift code verbatim; a mangled, untagged snippet yields broken output and lowers trust in the whole page.

recommendations.title: Add concrete rate-limit and latency numbers
recommendations.issue: "Please be mindful of rate limits" — no figure given
recommendations.change: State the actual limits, e.g. "Public endpoints are rate-limited to N requests/minute per IP; Intent endpoints with `x-api-key` allow M requests/minute." Add a typical response latency for Get Lane Latency.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes; "what are CCIP API rate limits" is a common query this page currently cannot answer.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased troubleshooting headings
recommendations.issue: Status codes are listed but not phrased as the questions devs type
recommendations.change: Add short H3s like "Why does my request return 404 Not Found?" (invalid message/intent ID) and "Why am I getting 500 errors?" (retry with exponential backoff), each answering in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Devs and agents query by symptom/error string; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add `APIReference`/`TechArticle` JSON-LD and a visible last-updated date
recommendations.change: Emit an `APIReference` (or `TechArticle`) block with `name`, `version` (2.0.0), and `dateModified`; surface a "Last updated" line on-page.
recommendations.why: Structured API metadata and freshness signals raise E-E-A-T and parse confidence for agents.

recommendations.title: Add one authoritative external link
recommendations.where: Lead paragraph, on first "Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol" mention
recommendations.change: Link the term to the canonical CCIP concept page and, if published, the OpenAPI/spec URL.
recommendations.why: Inline links to primary sources raise citation rate and let engines resolve the CCIP entity.

recommendations.title: State the concrete supported-chain and language specifics inline
recommendations.where: Multi-Chain Support and Quick Reference sections
recommendations.issue: Chain families shown only as icons; "9 languages" not enumerated
recommendations.change: Add text list "Supported chain families: EVM, Solana, Aptos, TON, Canton (5 total)" and name the 9 code-sample languages.
recommendations.why: Icon-only content is invisible to text-based retrieval; enumerated specifics are liftable.

antiPatterns: Corrupted/untagged code snippet (collapsed newlines in the curl example).
Vague quantifier without a number: "be mindful of rate limits," "Most … endpoints."
Icon-only Multi-Chain content with no text equivalent for text extractors.
offPageNotes: Site-level: add `APIReference` schema site-wide and an `llms.txt` to steer generative crawlers to canonical CCIP API pages.
Freshness cadence: surface `dateModified` from the CMS/build so engines see recency across the CCIP Tools section, not just this page.
